# Conditions, death, and dying

## Every SRD condition
- **Blinded:** cannot see and automatically fails sight-required checks; its attacks have Disadvantage and attacks against it have Advantage.
- **Charmed:** cannot attack the charmer or target it with damaging abilities or magical effects, and the charmer has Advantage on social checks involving it.
- **Deafened:** cannot hear and automatically fails checks requiring hearing.
- **Exhaustion:** each level worsens D20 Tests and reduces Speed; reaching the sixth level causes death, and finishing a Long Rest removes one level.
- **Frightened:** has Disadvantage on ability checks and attacks while the fear source is in line of sight and cannot willingly move closer to it.
- **Grappled:** Speed is zero, attacks against anyone but the grappler have Disadvantage, and the grappler can drag or carry it at extra movement cost unless size makes that easier; escape, release, an Incapacitated grappler, or separation beyond reach can end it.
- **Incapacitated:** cannot take an action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, loses Concentration, cannot speak, and has Disadvantage on Initiative if already Incapacitated when rolling.
- **Invisible:** is concealed from effects requiring sight, has Advantage on Initiative and attacks, and is attacked with Disadvantage unless the observer can somehow see it.
- **Paralyzed:** is Incapacitated with Speed zero, automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves, is attacked with Advantage, and a hit from within five feet is critical.
- **Petrified:** becomes an inanimate substance, is Incapacitated with Speed zero, is attacked with Advantage, automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves, resists all damage, and is immune to Poisoned.
- **Poisoned:** has Disadvantage on attacks and ability checks.
- **Prone:** can only crawl or spend half Speed to stand, attacks with Disadvantage, and is attacked with Advantage from within five feet but Disadvantage from farther away.
- **Restrained:** Speed is zero; its attacks have Disadvantage, attacks against it have Advantage, and its Dexterity saves have Disadvantage.
- **Stunned:** is Incapacitated, automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves, and is attacked with Advantage.
- **Unconscious:** is Incapacitated and Prone, drops held items, has Speed zero, automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves, is attacked with Advantage, takes critical hits from attacks within five feet, and is unaware.

## Death, dying, and unconsciousness
Dropping to zero Hit Points normally causes Unconscious and starts death saving throws, while excess damage can cause instant death. A death save is made at the start of the dying creature's turn: three successes stabilize it, three failures kill it, and taking damage while at zero adds failures as the rules specify. Regaining any Hit Points ends that dying state; a stable creature at zero remains Unconscious but stops making death saves and can eventually recover. Monsters normally die at zero, though a GM can apply the character procedure to an important one. A melee attacker reducing a creature to zero may instead knock it out under the SRD rule.
